title: Agent session state machine emitting contract state names
goal: A pure state machine that turns local runner signals into the product state names from CT-STATE-MAP and produces `agent.state` payloads that obey the contract's rate and dedupe rules; the client is the provider of these states.
scope_in: Reducer `nextState(current, signal, ctx): { state: AgentWireState; effects: Effect[] }` driven by signals from the bus (C025): prompt received, thinking start/stop, text streaming, tool requested (by tool name), approval needed/resolved, question asked, compaction start/end, turn result (success/error), process crash, interrupt, idle timers.

Tool-to-state mapping: Read/Glob/NotebookRead -> `reading-file`; Grep/WebSearch/WebFetch -> `searching`; Edit/MultiEdit -> `editing-file`; Write -> `creating-file` when the target does not exist else `editing-file`; Bash -> `running-command` (`deleting-file` only when the classifier of lane C016 flags a delete, via an optional `hints.deletesFiles`); Task/sub-agent -> `sub-agent`; background shell -> `background-task`; other tools -> `tool-running`; plan mode -> `planning`.

Transient states: `prompt-received` 600 ms, `approved`/`denied` 800 ms, `success` 2000 ms, then back to `idle` (all configurable constants, injected clock); `awaiting-approval` and `asking-question` persist until resolved; `thinking` escalates to `thinking-hard` after 15 s without output; `idle` becomes `sleeping` after 15 min inactivity.

Outcome mapping: turn failed -> `error`; subprocess died or runner crashed -> `crash`; non-fatal warnings (retry, rate-limit backoff) -> `warning`; test commands recognised by an injected `isTestCommand(argv)` hint finishing ok/fail -> `tests-pass`/`tests-fail`; merge conflict reported by the worktree lane -> `merge-conflict`; session snapshot being saved -> `saving`.

Emission gate `StateEmitter`: never re-emits an identical consecutive state; at most 2 emissions per agent per second (trailing-edge coalescing keeps the latest state); `since` is an RFC 3339 ms UTC timestamp of the change; output is the clear payload `{agent_id, state, since}` only.

Local-only UI states (connectivity, account, limits, social: `offline`, `reconnecting`, `online`, `auth-required`, `session-expired`, `rate-limited`, `quota-reached`, `cost-alert`, `context-full`, `teammate-*`, ...) are exposed via a separate `LocalUiState` type and never produced by this machine.
scope_out: Sending the `agent.state` frame: session layer lanes (this lane returns payloads and emits `agent:state_changed` on the bus).
Choosing animations or copy for states: lane C009 and TUI lanes.
Deriving connectivity/limits/social UI states: UI and net lanes.
build_against: Pure reducer tests with synthetic signal sequences and a fake clock; integration test wires the machine to the runner's `FakeSdkAdapter` (lane C013) over a bus (lane C025). Payloads are validated with the generated `agent.state` validator and `isAgentWireState` from lane C003.
interfaces: `type AgentWireState` (from `@centcom/protocol`, subset of the state-map keys); `type Signal = { type: 'prompt' } | { type: 'text_delta' } | { type: 'tool'; name: string; hints?: { deletesFiles?: boolean; isTest?: boolean; createsFile?: boolean } } | { type: 'approval'; phase: 'needed'|'approved'|'denied' } | { type: 'question' } | { type: 'compaction'; phase: 'start'|'end' } | { type: 'turn_end'; ok: boolean } | { type: 'crash' } | { type: 'interrupt' } | { type: 'conflict' } | { type: 'saving'; phase: 'start'|'end' } | { type: 'tick' }`
`createStateMachine(deps: { agentId: AgentId; clock: Clock; bus: AgentBus; timings?: Partial<Timings> }): { signal(s: Signal): void; current(): AgentWireState; dispose(): void }`

`createStateEmitter(deps: { clock: Clock; send: (p: AgentStatePayload) => void }): { push(agentId, state): void; flush(): void }` with `AgentStatePayload = { agent_id: string; state: AgentWireState; since: string }`.
acceptance: Every value the machine can produce is a member of `AGENT_WIRE_STATES` (exhaustive test over all signals x states: 0 violations) and a key of contracts/state-map.json.

Sequence prompt -> tool Read -> tool Edit -> approval needed -> approved -> turn_end ok produces exactly: prompt-received, thinking, reading-file, editing-file, awaiting-approval, approved, (800 ms) editing-file/thinking, success, (2000 ms) idle with the fake clock.
Emitter dedupe: pushing `thinking` 5 times produces 1 send; 10 distinct states pushed within 1 s produce at most 2 sends for that second and the last send carries the latest state.
Each send payload validates against the generated `agent.state` clear-payload schema and contains no fields other than `agent_id`, `state`, `since`.
`thinking` with no output for 15 s transitions to `thinking-hard`; idle for 15 min transitions to `sleeping`; a new prompt wakes it (all fake-clock).
Crash signal from any state yields `crash` and the machine stays terminal until `dispose`; interrupt returns to `idle` within one tick.
A static test confirms the module never references the strings `offline`, `reconnecting`, `rate-limited`, `quota-reached`, `teammate-joins` as outputs.
tests: integration.test.ts with FakeSdkAdapter, property test: random signal streams never emit an invalid state or exceed 2/s.
guardrails: MUST emit only names that exist in contracts/state-map.json and only the agent-level subset; MUST NOT invent states or localise them.
MUST enforce <= 2 `agent.state` payloads per agent per second and MUST NOT re-send identical consecutive states (CT-STATE-MAP rule 2).
Payload MUST be the clear fields only (`agent_id`, `state`, `since`); MUST NOT attach tool names, paths or commands.
MUST NOT derive local-only UI states here; connectivity and limit states stay out of `agent.state`.
State names are not user-facing copy: no text strings in this lane.
failure_modes: Out-of-order signals (approval resolved without needed) -> ignored with a debug log, state unchanged.
Clock drift/backwards -> `since` still non-decreasing per agent (clamped).
notes: CONTRACT GAP: CT-STATE-MAP says which categories travel as `agent.state` but the 'outcome (agent-level)' wording does not list which of celebrate, ci-*, pr-* count; this lane emits only success, error, crash, warning, tests-pass, tests-fail, merge-conflict, deploying (when a hint is given) and saving. `context-full` is under 'limits' (client-local) so it is surfaced as a local UI state, not on the wire. Event schema `agent.state.since` semantics ('state started at') assumed.
